findings.title: Gap-fill interpolate(limit=3) fabricates WSE in long gaps instead of skipping them
findings.description: _fine_regular_grid is documented as 'interpolate internal gaps up to this wide' (FINE_FILL_GAP_KM = 0.3 km = 3 bins), but pandas Series.interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') does NOT restrict filling to gaps <= 3 bins: it fills the FIRST 3 NaNs of EVERY interior gap regardless of gap length (and only from the left, since limit_direction defaults to 'forward'). Those filled bins lie on the straight chord between the gap's endpoints, so the per-pass Theil-Sen slope near the upstream edge of every long coverage gap is the chord slope across the whole gap, not a measured local slope. The identical line exists in dashboard_swot.py:351, so both the Fine-Scale Slope tab and thesis Fig 9 (core.finescale_slope_profile) consume fabricated data.
findings.failure_scenario: Demonstrated: pd.Series([1,nan*6,8]).interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') -> [1,2,3,4,nan,nan,nan,8], i.e. 3 fabricated points inside a 6-bin gap. Reproducing the full pipeline on batch_outputs/master_all_data.parquet (open-water, 2025-04-17 excluded, res=0.5 km, xmax=34): 149 of 213 reach-passes contain interior gaps > 0.3 km, injecting 2,532 fabricated 100-m bins into the Theil-Sen fits. Versus a corrected fill (only gaps <= 3 bins), the aggregated median profile (min_passes=3, exactly Fig 9) changes at 211/338 Uyak bins by > 1 cm/km, worst-case 124 cm/km (Uyak at 5.0-5.2 km: 253 -> 326 cm/km at 5.0 km, which is inside the 1-5 km headline window edge); Kanektok worst-case 62 cm/km at 30.1 km. Per-pass 1-5 km window slopes ('Slope over time' view) shift up to 22 cm/km and the >=80%-coverage gated pass count changes (Uyak 42 -> 30). The headline medians are robust (Kanektok 258.9 -> 258.0; Uyak 1-5 km median unchanged; paired advantage moves ~1 cm/km), but the published Fig 9 profile curve is materially wrong at sparse-coverage locations.
findings.suggested_fix: After the limited interpolate, mask back to NaN any filled values that belong to a NaN run longer than max_gap (compute run lengths on the pre-fill NaN mask), or fill via a run-length-aware routine. Apply identically in dashboard_swot.py:351 and core.py:270 to keep them in lockstep.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Code is exactly as described. thesis_figures/core.py:262-271 (_fine_regular_grid) reindexes one pass onto a contiguous 0.1 km index, then `s = s.interpolate(limit=max_gap, limit_area="inside")` with max_gap=3 (FINE_FILL_GAP_KM=0.3 / FINE_BASE_BIN_KM=0.1). The docstring/constant comment at core.py:219 says 'per pass, interpolate internal gaps up to this wide', but pandas `limit` caps *consecutive* fills, it does not skip longer runs. Verified on the installed pandas 2.3.2: pd.Series([1,nan*6,8]).interpolate(limit=3, limit_area='inside') -> [1,2,3,4,nan,nan,nan,8]. Those 3 values lie on the chord across the whole 6-bin gap. The filled bins are then indistinguishable from observations to _fine_slope_theilsen (core.py:241-252 only checks np.isfinite), so they enter the 0.5 km sliding Theil-Sen fit. Fig 9 (make_figures.py:874) calls core.finescale_slope_profile directly, so the published figure consumes them. Severity high (not critical): the canonical headline numbers barely move, but the plotted profile curve is materially wrong in places, including inside the bifurcation zoom panel.
findings.reproduction: Reimplemented the exact core.finescale_slope_profile pipeline (same SQL, npix>=30, xmax=34, res=0.5, min_passes=3) on batch_outputs/master_all_data.parquet with open-water months and 2025-04-17 excluded, comparing the current fill against a run-length-aware fill (only NaN runs <= 3 bins filled). Output: 'series=213 affected(long gaps)=149 fabricated_bins=2532 intended_fills=3974'; Kanektok |diff|>1 cm/km at 82/338 bins, worst 62.3 at 30.1 km (83.8 -> 21.5); Uyak |diff|>1 cm/km at 211/338 bins, worst 123.7 at 5.1 km (271.5 -> 395.2). 1-5 km medians: Kanektok 258.8 -> 258.0, Uyak 227.5 -> 227.5. Per-pass 80%-coverage gate: Uyak 42 -> 30 gated passes, Kanektok 89 -> 83. Every number in the finding's failure scenario reproduced within rounding. findings.title: abs() of signed quantiles produces a band that can exclude the plotted median
findings.description: finescale_slope_profile (and dashboard _fine_aggregate, dashboard_swot.py:446) computes q25/q75 of the SIGNED per-pass slopes, then plots steepness as lo=min(|q25|,|q75|), hi=max(|q25|,|q75|), med=|median|. When per-pass slopes straddle zero (q25 < 0 < q75), |quantile| is not a quantile of |slope|: both |q25| and |q75| can exceed |median|, so the plotted median falls BELOW the band's lower edge and the shaded 'IQR' is no longer a 25-75% interval of anything.
findings.failure_scenario: Real data (full archive, exact Fig 9 pipeline): Uyak Creek bins at 33.5, 33.7, 33.9, 34.0 km (all with n >= 3, so plotted in Fig 9's full panel and the dashboard aggregate view) have plotted medians of 7.2, 8.6, 2.0, 12.8 cm/km sitting below band lower edges of 14.9, 8.8, 19.1, 14.0 cm/km; Kanektok has 2 such bins (33.9, 34.0 km). Synthetic: signed slopes [-2, +0.1, +1] -> q25=-0.95, q75=0.55, median=0.1; plotted band [0.55, 0.95] excludes plotted med 0.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Where the signed IQR straddles zero, clamp lo to min(lo, med) (or 0), or plot signed slope with a sign-flip note; alternatively compute the band as quantiles of |slope| but keep med=|median(signed)| documented as such.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Code confirmed at thesis_figures/core.py:331-337 and dashboard_swot.py:440-446: q25/q75 are taken on the SIGNED slope matrix, then a25=|q25|, a75=|q75|, lo=min(a25,a75), hi=max(a25,a75), med=|median|. Where the signed distribution straddles zero this is not a quantile of |slope|, and med can fall outside [lo,hi]. make_figures.py:build_fig9 draws ax.fill_between(g, lo, hi) and ax.plot(g, med) on the same axes, so the defect is visible as a median line outside its own band in panel (a) (panel b is 0-8 km and is unaffected). Downgraded from medium to low: only 11 of 676 plotted bins straddle zero and all of them are beyond 27 km, i.e. in the tidal tail far downstream of the bifurcation; 6 bins actually show med<lo; no headline number, no reach-average, and no near-bifurcation conclusion depends on them.
findings.reproduction: Ran thesis_figures.core.finescale_slope_profile() with defaults and checked med<lo. Kanektok: 2 bins - 33.9 km (med 6.9, lo 22.7, hi 34.3, n=116) and 34.0 km (med 14.1, lo 31.6, hi 41.4, n=113). Uyak: 4 bins - 33.5 km (7.2 vs lo 14.9), 33.7 km (8.6 vs 8.8), 33.9 km (1.9 vs 19.1), 34.0 km (12.8 vs 14.0). Matches the finding's list (its 2.0 vs my 1.9 at 33.9 km is rounding). Separately counted sign-straddling bins (q25<0<q75, n>=3): Kanektok 3 (29.9, 33.9, 34.0 km), Uyak 8 (27.6, 32.1, 33.5-34.0 km) out of 338 plotted bins each. No bin has med>hi.

findings.title: calculate_slope_profile smooths across missing 100-m bins as if adjacent
findings.description: calculate_slope_profile (identical in thesis_figures/core.py:199) drops empty 100-m bins from bin_medians and then runs gaussian_filter1d(sigma=smooth_km/bin_size) on the COMPACTED array, so bins on opposite sides of an unobserved stretch are treated as 0.1 km apart. np.interp then linearly bridges the gap on the physical axis, and np.gradient reports a smooth, plausible-looking slope through river that was never observed, while also distorting slopes adjacent to the gap (the effective smoothing window in km shrinks across gaps).
findings.failure_scenario: Synthetic demonstration: uniform true slope 200 cm/km with a 3 km unobserved gap (bins 100-129 missing) -> computed |slope| inside/near the gap is 1-32 cm/km, i.e. up to 99% low. Full-archive pooled data currently has ZERO missing interior bins for both rivers (verified), so thesis Fig 8 is unaffected -- but the dashboard runs this on arbitrary pass selections (line 2714 with the user's where_clause; line 1449 on the 15k-point viz_df sample), and partial-coverage passes exist (e.g. 2026-07-09 Kanektok images only 45 of ~350 bins), so a multi-pass selection with disjoint coverage produces confidently wrong slope curves over unobserved reaches.
findings.suggested_fix: Reindex the binned medians onto the full regular grid with NaNs, smooth with a NaN-aware Gaussian (normalized convolution), and return NaN slope where local coverage is absent instead of interpolating across gaps.
findings.verifier_reasoning: dashboard_swot.py:233-275 (and the verbatim port at thesis_figures/core.py:180-205) groups by 100 m bin, so absent bins simply do not appear in bin_medians; gaussian_filter1d(sigma=smooth_km/bin_size=20 bins) is then applied to that COMPACTED array, treating bins on either side of an unobserved stretch as 0.1 km apart. np.interp maps back to the true physical axis, so an elevation step that is physically spread over kilometres is smeared over the smoothing kernel as if it were local — flattening the derivative near and inside the gap. The finding is honest about scope: I confirmed thesis Fig 8 is unaffected, and confirmed the dashboard path is affected in ordinary use. Medium is the right severity: no thesis number changes; the dashboard's Slope Profile tab and the per-point interval_slope column (line 1449) are wrong for gappy selections.
findings.reproduction: (a) Pooled all-passes 100 m bins have ZERO interior missing bins for both rivers (Kanektok 349 bins, Uyak 359 bins) — Fig 8 confirmed unaffected. (b) Per pass-reach series, 120 of 354 have >=1 interior missing bin (57 of 238 open-water; 15 with >10 missing). Longest single-pass interior gaps: Uyak 2023-12-03 and 2023-12-15 at 22 bins (2.2 km), Uyak 2026-01-25 with 130 missing bins. (c) Compared the shipped compacted math against a NaN-aware normalized-convolution version on the true physical grid for single-pass selections: Uyak 2026-01-25 max |slope| difference 415 cm/km at 12.6 km (33.7 vs 448.9), mean 108; Uyak 2026-04-18 max 374 cm/km; Uyak 2023-12-15 max 430 cm/km. (d) Synthetic uniform 200 cm/km with a 3 km unobserved gap: compacted reports 10-29 cm/km inside the gap (finding claimed 1-32), i.e. ~90% low. (e) The specific 2026-07-09 Kanektok claim checks out on coverage (45 bins) though that pass is contiguous, so it only produces gaps in combination with other partial passes.

findings.title: Cache keys never capture the data version: url_version is a constant, so the documented cache-busting cannot fire
findings.description: The comment at 569–571 says the connection cache key (url_version) 'invalidates when the data source changes', and compute_finescale_pass_matrix's docstring says 'url_version keys the cache to the deployed data version'. But url_version is always the module constant REMOTE_PARQUET_URL — it can only change via a code edit, which redeploys and clears all caches anyway. The project's documented data-swap workflow (MEMORY: 'stable filename — swap data without code changes' on GitHub Release v2.0-data) changes the bytes behind the SAME URL, busting nothing. Meanwhile load_detrend_frame (line 200), load_dem_profile (626), load_dem_points (647), load_reference_gradient (1064), load_refgrad_decomposition (1078) and load_metadata (1108) have no data-version key at all — their outputs depend entirely on the data behind _con (which is excluded from the key), bounded only by ttl=86400.
findings.failure_scenario: Swap dashboard_data.parquet in the GitHub release (or, locally, re-run SWOT_Pull.py adding new partition files while the app is running): the DuckDB views read the new data immediately, so uncached queries (viz_df, stats_df, diff_query, slope_query) reflect the new archive, while every @st.cache_data loader above serves frames computed from the OLD data for up to 24 hours. Tabs then disagree: e.g. the Hydraulic Gradient reference values and the DEM profile show stale numbers next to fresh profile/difference charts, and load_metadata hides newly ingested pass dates from the welcome page for up to a day.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive a real data-version token (e.g. HTTP ETag/Last-Modified of the release asset, or max(Pass_Date)+row count for local partitions) at connection time and pass it as a plain cache-key argument to every data-dependent @st.cache_data loader; or correct the comments/docstrings to state that ttl=86400 is the only staleness bound.
findings.verifier_reasoning: All code claims check out. REMOTE_PARQUET_URL is a module constant (dashboard_swot.py:27). get_database_connection(url_version=REMOTE_PARQUET_URL) at line 573 is called with no argument at line 3841, and compute_finescale_pass_matrix is called at line 2815-2816 with the literal constant, so url_version is invariant at runtime — it can only change via a source edit, which on Streamlit Cloud restarts the app and clears all caches anyway. The comment at 569-571 and the docstring at 381-382 therefore describe a mechanism that cannot fire. The other @st.cache_data loaders have no data-version key at all: load_detrend_frame (200) keys on where_clause+method only, load_dem_profile (626), load_dem_points (647), load_reference_gradient (1065), load_refgrad_decomposition (1079) and load_metadata (1109) take only the underscore-prefixed _con, so their cache key is empty and ttl=86400 is the sole staleness bound. Meanwhile the uncached per-selection queries (viz_df, stats_df, slope_query at 2690, the fine-scale SQL at 383) hit the DuckDB view directly. The documented deployment workflow is precisely 'stable filename — swap data without code changes', so a data swap yields up to 24 h of cross-tab disagreement (stale reference gradient / DEM profile / pass list next to fresh profile and slope charts). Medium is correct: it produces stale-but-not-fabricated numbers, is time-bounded, and requires an admin data swap — not critical, but more than cosmetic because the comment actively asserts a protection that does not exist.
findings.reproduction: Static verification only (the failure requires swapping the remote release asset, which I must not do). grep confirmed the only call sites: line 3841 `con = get_database_connection()` (no arg) and lines 2815-2816 passing the REMOTE_PARQUET_URL constant; no other assignment to url_version exists anywhere in the file.

findings.title: Fine-scale IQR band from abs() of signed quantiles is wrong where slopes straddle zero; median line plots outside its own band
findings.description: _fine_aggregate computes signed q25/q75 across passes, then derives the plotted band as [min(|q25|,|q75|), max(|q25|,|q75|)] and the line as |median| (lines 444-446). When per-pass slopes straddle zero (flat/tidal downstream bins), this is not the IQR of |slope|: the band excludes zero, misses the true absolute-slope quartiles, and can exclude the plotted median itself.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced the full compute_finescale_pass_matrix + _fine_aggregate pipeline on the local archive (all passes). 12 displayed core bins (n>=3) have q25<0<q75, and in 7 of them the plotted median lies OUTSIDE the plotted band — e.g. Uyak 33.6 km: plotted median 6.5 cm/km with band [16.4, 36.8], while the correct |slope| stats are median 27.2, IQR [13.1, 48.9]; Kanektok 33.9 km: plotted median 6.8 with band [42.0, 44.5], correct median 44.1, IQR [17.6, 93.5]. The 1-5 km near-bifurcation headline numbers are NOT affected (slopes there are far from zero).

findings.title: Temporal tab 'Lower river (<=18 km)' / 'Upper river (>18 km)' labels are geographically inverted

findings.title: MAD outlier filter on raw WSE amputates the upstream half of Uyak Creek on 28% of dates and misses real outliers
findings.description: `calculate_mad_outliers` (line 121) is applied to RAW per-reach WSE (line 316-320), not to residuals from the along-river trend. The reach has ~66 m of real relief over 35 km, so median/MAD are dominated by the trend and by the pixel-density distribution along the profile. Two failure modes, both demonstrated on real archive data: (a) When density is downstream-weighted (narrow upstream creek, wide lower river — typical for Uyak), the median sits near the low downstream WSE, MAD is small, and the band `median ± 5.19*MAD` classifies ALL legitimate upstream water as outliers, deleting entire river reaches. (b) When density is uniform (Kanektok), MAD ≈ 14 m, the band is ±73 m, and genuine multi-meter outliers pass untouched. The `MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER=5` safety check (line 324) permits removing thousands of points as long as 5 survive. Effect on published numbers: 46 of 167 dates with both rivers have Uyak's coverage start >1 km behind Kanektok's on the identical repeating orbit; 7 of the 67 gated open-water Uyak passes feeding the canonical reference gradient are amputated at 1-3 km (inside the REFGRAD_MAX_START_KM=3.0 gate), and their median |Theil-Sen slope| is 184.6 cm/km vs 192.0 for the 60 clean passes — i.e., the exact steep-reach-clipping bias the coverage gate was designed to exclude, depressing the published Uyak 191.7 cm/km. The amputation is spread across all months, so it also contaminates the seasonal/temporal analysis and the Kanektok-vs-Uyak gated-pass-count asymmetry (88 vs 67).

Same date Kanektok: raw MAD band ±72.8 m removes 0 points while residual-domain finds 178 outliers up to 11.8 m off-trend. Archive-wide fingerprint across the 45 repeats of identical pass 026: Uyak coverage start jumps between 0.31 and 25.26 km date-to-date with wse_max clipped in lockstep (e.g., 2023-11-03: starts 20.0 km, wse_max 19.15 m, 201-413 px at the first surviving nodes and zero above, while Kanektok has 660-780 px per node in the same swath region — the region was imaged; only a WSE-thresholding step can cut at a wse isoline, and MAD is the only such step in the pipeline).
findings.suggested_fix: Detrend first: fit a robust along-distance trend (Theil-Sen on 1-km node medians, same model as compute_reference_gradient) per reach-pass, then apply the modified-z MAD test to residuals. Also cap the fraction removable (e.g., skip if >10% flagged) instead of the 5-point floor. Re-pull or re-filter from raw granules — the daily CSVs are post-amputation, so the deleted points are not recoverable from checkpoints.
findings.verifier_reasoning: calculate_mad_outliers (SWOT_Pull.py:121-145) is applied at lines 316-320 to the raw per-reach WSE of a granule, never to residuals from an along-river trend, over a reach with ~66 m of real relief; the keep band is median +/- 5.19*MAD and MIN_POINTS_AFTER_FILTER=5 (line 324) allows arbitrarily large removals. findings.title: geolocation_qual.astype(int) crashes on partially-NaN flag column, silently discarding the whole granule
findings.description: xarray decodes _FillValue pixels of geolocation_qual to NaN (float column). The guard `df_exact['geolocation_qual'].notna().any()` (line 292) enters the filter branch when ANY value is valid, but `.astype(int)` on line 293 raises `IntCastingNaNError` if ANY value is NaN. So a granule where even one in-polygon pixel has fill geolocation_qual (mixed with valid pixels) throws, is caught by the catch-all `except` at line 359, prints one scrolling '❌ Failed' line, and returns None — the entire granule (all reaches, all tiles that date) is dropped from the archive. Because no CSV is written, every future resume run re-downloads and re-fails identically: a permanent, effectively silent hole in the record. The guard's existence shows partial-NaN was anticipated; the cast defeats it.
findings.failure_scenario: Constructed and ran the exact failing case under the environment's pandas 2.3.2: `s = pd.Series([3.0, np.nan, 8388608.0]); s.notna().any() -> True; (s.astype(int) & 8388608)` raises `IntCastingNaNError: Cannot convert non-finite values (NA or inf) to integer`. In process_granule this propagates to the outer except -> granule skipped with only a tqdm line; main() counts it neither as processed nor as failed in the summary (line 596).
findings.suggested_fix: Treat NaN qual as its own category, e.g. `q = df_exact['geolocation_qual']; xover_mask = q.notna() & (q.fillna(0).astype('int64') & XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK == 0)` (or keep NaN-qual pixels explicitly if that is the intended policy). Same latent pattern applies to any future use of classification_qual/height_cor_xover_qual.
findings.verifier_reasoning: The code defect is exactly as described. SWOT_Pull.py:292 guards with notna().any() but line 293 does df_exact['geolocation_qual'].astype(int) & XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK, which raises IntCastingNaNError under the installed pandas 2.3.2 if a single value is NaN; the exception propagates out of the with-block to the catch-all except at line 359, prints one tqdm line, returns None, writes no CSV, and main()'s summary (line 596) counts it as neither processed nor skipped, so a resume run re-downloads and re-fails identically. The trigger is real in principle: CMR UMM-Var records /pixel_cloud/geolocation_qual as uint with _FillValue 4294967295 and valid max 4193841279, so xarray's default mask_and_scale yields a float64 array that carries NaN wherever a pixel is filled. What I could not establish is that filled pixels actually occur inside these polygons: the pipeline succeeded on ~190 dates x 2 reaches, and only 5-6 in-range dates with a river-covering pass produced no CSV (2024-01-15, 2024-01-25, 2024-05-09, 2024-06-29, 2025-01-13, 2025-05-09), which are equally explicable by never-requested date ranges or download failures. I also disagree with one supporting argument: the notna().any() guard exists for the variable-absent case (the dict comprehension at line 249 sets the column to scalar np.nan when 'geolocation_qual' not in ds), not because partial NaN was anticipated. Downgraded high -> medium: real latent bug with a genuinely silent and permanent failure mode, but zero demonstrated occurrences and an evidently very low incidence.
findings.reproduction: pandas 2.3.2: pd.Series([3.0, nan, 8388608.0]).notna().any() -> True; (s.astype(int) & 8388608) -> IntCastingNaNError. findings.title: Geoid hull fallback puts up to 0.34 m datum error into 36,803 DEM profile points, concentrated at the Uyak mouth
findings.description: build_geoid_interpolator() builds a LinearNDInterpolator over the convex hull of (subsampled) SWOT pixel locations; every DEM pixel outside that hull silently gets the constant FALLBACK_GEOID = 13.46 m. The out-of-hull points are not scattered — they are exactly where the geoid deviates most from 13.46: rebuilding the interpolator from batch_outputs/data/*.csv and applying it to dem_river_elevations.parquet shows 36,803/2,485,204 points (1.48%) get the fallback, 34,600 of them at Uyak dist_km 32-36 (true geoid ~13.21 m, so wse biased LOW by ~0.25 m) and ~1,900 at dist_km 0-1 (true geoid ~13.79 m, wse biased HIGH by ~0.33 m). The 0.5 km binned-median profile the dashboard draws is contaminated: the terminal Uyak bin at 36.0 km is 84% fallback points and its median is 0.24 m too low (measured: 1.739 m vs corrected 1.982 m); bins 33.5-35.5 are 12-33% contaminated. Any per-point DEM-vs-SWOT residual analysis over the coastal Uyak reach inherits a systematic ~0.25 m tilt.
findings.failure_scenario: Ran DEM_Pull's interpolator rebuild against batch_outputs/data CSVs and evaluated on dem_river_elevations.parquet: 36,803 NaN (out-of-hull) points; nearest-grid true geoid gives fallback error median +0.247 m at the coast, -0.336 m at the anchor. Recomputing the Uyak 36.0 km bin median with the corrected geoid shifts it +0.243 m — the published DEM profile's last bin shows an artificial ~0.24 m dip at the river mouth.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the constant fallback with nearest-neighbour extrapolation of the SWOT geoid grid (e.g. scipy.interpolate.NearestNDInterpolator for out-of-hull points), or clamp out-of-hull points to the nearest hull value; the geoid is smooth so NN extrapolation is accurate to <2 cm here.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Code reads as described: build_geoid_interpolator (DEM_Pull.py:131-163) bins ~11 sampled SWOT CSVs to a 0.005 deg grid and wraps it in LinearNDInterpolator (NaN outside the convex hull); process_dataframe (178-187) replaces every NaN with the constant FALLBACK_GEOID = 13.46 m and only prints a count. I rebuilt the interpolator from batch_outputs/data/*_data.csv exactly as the code does (1015 grid points, geoid range 13.202-13.796 m) and evaluated it on all 2,485,204 rows of batch_outputs/dem_river_elevations.parquet: 36,803 NaN (1.4809%), of which 34,586 sit at Uyak dist_km 31-36 (nearest-neighbour true geoid 13.203-13.219 m, so the 13.46 constant pushes wse ~0.25 m LOW) and 1,884 at dist_km 0-0.5 on both rivers (true 13.796 m, wse ~0.34 m HIGH). Recomputing the dashboard's own binning (ROUND(dist_km/0.5)*0.5, MEDIAN(wse) — dashboard_swot.py:632-643) with a nearest-neighbour-corrected geoid: the terminal Uyak 36.0 km bin is 83.7% fallback and its median moves +0.2429 m (1.7394 -> 1.9823); bins 32.5-35.5 are 6-33% fallback with +0.002 to +0.052 m shifts. Every figure in the finding reproduces to three decimals. Severity trimmed to medium: the DEM parquet feeds thesis_figures (config.DEM_PATH) and the dashboard DEM tab, so the artificial mouth dip is real, but the visible product effect is one 0.5 km terminal bin plus centimetre-level shifts elsewhere, and the arc cross-section / superelevation pipeline is unaffected (build_arc_B.py samples the raster with geoid_m from swot_arc_reference.parquet, not this parquet).
findings.reproduction: Rebuilt DEM_Pull's LinearNDInterpolator from batch_outputs/data/*_data.csv (files[::18], 11 files), applied to dem_river_elevations.parquet: 36,803/2,485,204 NaN (1.4809%); NearestNDInterpolator on the same grid gives true geoid 13.796 at dist 0-1 and 13.203-13.219 at Uyak dist 31-36. Re-binned at 0.5 km: Uyak 36.0 km bin n=5228, fallback fraction 0.837, median 1.739 -> 1.982 (+0.243 m); Uyak 35.0 bin +0.052 m; Kanektok 0.5 bin -0.007 m.

findings.title: Headline superelevation silently falls back from SWOT-median stage to DEM stage per-radius, mixing stage bases that differ by up to 1.3 m
findings.description: `ch['kan_superelev_m'] = ch['kan_superelev_med_m'].fillna(ch['kan_superelev_dem_m'])` (and the Uyak twin) splices two quantities with different stage definitions into one unflagged column: the SWOT-median-stage superelevation and the DEM-mosaic-stage superelevation. On the committed data these differ per-arc by -1.30 to +1.01 m (Kanektok) and -0.78 to +0.69 m (Uyak) where both exist. Today the fallback fires on 0 rows (only R=3.0 lacks the SWOT median, and fp_ref is also NaN there), but the guard is MIN_PASSES=8 per (river, radius) in swot_arc_reference.py — any rebuild with thinner coverage (e.g. from the smaller swot_apr_jul_2025_2026.parquet candidate, or extended radii) silently produces a superelevation-vs-radius curve whose level jumps by up to ~1 m at the radii where the source switches, with no flag column distinguishing the two regimes.

The magnitude claim holds on the committed data: across arcB_channels.parquet (64 arcs) med-minus-dem ranges -1.302..+1.007 m for the Kanektok and -0.775..+0.687 m for the Uyak. The gate is MIN_PASSES = 8 evaluated per (river, radius) in swot_arc_reference.py:101, and SWOT_CANDIDATES lists the smaller swot_apr_jul_2025_2026.parquet as a fallback source, so the switch is reachable on a rebuild. But the finding concedes, and I verified, that the fallback fires on exactly 0 rows today: the only NaN median is R = 3.0, where fp_ref_m is NaN too, so both the med and dem superelevations are NaN and fillna is a no-op. With zero current effect and a trigger that requires swapping the SWOT source or extending the radius grid, this is a latent robustness/labelling defect — low, not medium.

The 2025-04-17 ice pass (~10.8k rows; reach gradients 236/224 cm/km vs medians ~192/196) silently re-enters master_all_data_part_*.parquet, which dashboard_swot.py and temporal_analysis.py read unfiltered — means/bands/extremes on the dashboard and any re-run temporal stats are contaminated by the pass that was formally QC-excluded. findings.verifier_reasoning: Code reading confirms every element. SWOT_Pull.py:64-76 defines KNOWN_BAD_PASSES={'2025-04-17': ...}; SWOT_Pull.py:485-495 applies it inside rebuild_master_from_daily_csvs() BEFORE writing master_all_data.csv/.parquet and the part_*.parquet partitions, and SWOT_Pull.py:557 then calls compute_reference_gradient(final_df) on the already-filtered frame (the comment at 486-487 explicitly calls this the 'single filter point'). rebuild_master.py:14 imports only `KEEP_COLUMNS, ROWS_PER_CHUNK`; line 40 does `final_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)` over `sorted(DATA_DIR.glob('*_data.csv'))` with no Pass_Date filter anywhere in the file, and the file contains no reference to KNOWN_BAD_PASSES or compute_reference_gradient. Neither dashboard_swot.py nor temporal_analysis.py contains any pass-exclusion list (grep for KNOWN_BAD_PASSES/EXCLUDED_PASSES/'2025-04-17' hits only SWOT_Pull.py, thesis_figures/config.py:66-71 and thesis_figures/core.py:33-48), so they consume the partitions unfiltered and would silently inherit the re-added pass; only thesis_figures is independently protected. findings.title: Thesis labels Uyak seasonal slope p=0.033 as 'Not Significant'; pipeline reports it significant
findings.description: temporal_analysis.py:_mwu (line 143) labels any p<0.05 'significant', and the archived run produced p=0.0327 for the Uyak pooled seasonal slope contrast (temporal_results/temporal_analysis_results.json: Q1_slope_pooled, Uyak_Creek, p_slope=0.0327, n_high=10, n_low=15). The script therefore printed '-> seasonal slope swing +2.3 cm/km [p=0.033 (significant, n=10 vs 15)]', and the dashboard's _fmt_p (dashboard_swot.py:3483) renders it '0.033 *' (starred as significant). But the thesis table (Project_Info/'Masters Thesis (6).pdf', seasonal-slope table) prints 'Not Significant (p=0.033)' for exactly this comparison — a direct contradiction of the pipeline's own stated alpha=0.05 convention, in a published table. TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md:101 calls the same result 'marginally so'. Three artifacts, three different verdicts for one number.
findings.failure_scenario: Ran pdftotext on Project_Info/'Masters Thesis (6).pdf' and grepped: the table row reads 'Uyak | 193.5 cm/km | 191.2 cm/km | +2.3 cm/km | Not Significant (p=0.033)'. Reproduced the script's output path: p=0.0327 -> line 143 assigns 'significant'. A committee member checking the table against alpha=0.05 (or against the live dashboard, which stars it) sees the thesis asserting the opposite of its own analysis code.
findings.suggested_fix: Either correct the thesis label to 'significant (p=0.033)' with the existing caveat that the effect is small and year-inconsistent, or explicitly justify 'not significant' via a multiple-comparison correction (with ~14 MWU tests, Bonferroni alpha ~0.0036 would make it n.s.) and state that correction in both the thesis and TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md; make _mwu/_fmt_p and the thesis use the same rule.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Every factual claim checks out. temporal_analysis.py:136-144 `_mwu` sets `sig = 'significant' if p < 0.05 else 'not significant'` with no correction; temporal_results/temporal_analysis_results.json Q1_seasonal contains {'question':'Q1_slope_pooled','reach':'Uyak_Creek','n_high':10,'n_low':15,'slope_high':193.536,'slope_low':191.198,'dslope_cm_km':2.34,'p_slope':0.0327}, so the script's printed line reads '(significant, n=10 vs 15)'. dashboard_swot.py:3483-3486 `_fmt_p` appends ' *' for p<0.05, rendering '0.033 *'. pdftotext of Project_Info/'Masters Thesis (6).pdf' lines 511-512 gives 'Uyak | 193.5 cm/km | 191.2 cm/km | +2.3 cm/km | Not Significant ($$p=0.033$$)'. TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md:100-103 calls the same result 'marginally so ... (p=0.03)'. So three artifacts do give three different verdicts for one p-value, and grep shows the word 'bonferroni/holm/fdr/multiple compar' appears in NONE of temporal_analysis.py, TEMPORAL_ANALYSIS.md, dashboard_swot.py or the thesis text — no correction is stated anywhere that would justify the thesis label. Severity downgraded from critical to medium: no computed number is wrong, the disputed effect is +2.3 cm/km (~1% of a ~192 cm/km gradient) and the thesis's label errs conservatively, so the chapter's conclusion (seasonal stage-invariance) is unaffected either way. Also note the finding slightly overstates the contradiction: the thesis never states an alpha or names Mann-Whitney at all (grep for '0.05|alpha|Mann' in the extracted text returns nothing), so the conflict is across artifacts rather than internal to the thesis. It remains a real, visible inconsistency — a reader comparing the table to the live dashboard sees '0.033 *' against 'Not Significant'.
findings.reproduction: pdftotext -layout 'Project_Info/Masters Thesis (6).pdf' then grep -> line 511/512 as quoted; python json load of temporal_results/temporal_analysis_results.json -> p_slope 0.0327, n_high 10, n_low 15; grep -i for correction keywords across the four artifacts -> zero hits; grep '0.05|alpha|Mann' in thesis text -> zero hits.

findings.title: ~14 uncorrected Mann-Whitney tests and an uncertainty-free point-median Q3 verdict
findings.description: The run performs 16 MWU tests (Q1 pooled slope x2, Q1 WSE per year x6 of which 2 return NaN for n<3, Q2 x4, Q3 x4 — 14 with valid p), each judged at raw alpha=0.05 in _mwu (line 143) with no family-wise correction, and results are exported to JSON/dashboard/thesis. Separately, the Q3 'exceeds/within natural baseline' verdict (lines 277-279) is a bare comparison of two point medians, abs(dwse) > abs(baseline_dwse), computed from n=4 vs ~4 June passes, with no CI/bootstrap — a sign flip in either small-sample median flips the published verdict. Note the interaction with the thesis finding above: the only raw-significant temporal result (Uyak p=0.033) would be n.s. under any family-wise correction, but no such correction is stated anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: With 14 tests at alpha=0.05 the expected false-positive count under the global null is ~0.7; the single p=0.033 hit is exactly the pattern multiplicity produces, yet the JSON/dashboard star it as significant while the thesis (without stating a correction) calls it not significant. For Q3: temporal_analysis_results.json Q3_typhoon rows carry 'wse_vs_baseline' verdicts derived from medians of 3-4 passes; moving one 2026 June pass by ~0.1 m flips 'within' to 'exceeds'.
findings.suggested_fix: Report Holm/Bonferroni-adjusted p-values (or FDR) in the JSON and docs, and replace the Q3 verdict with a bootstrap CI on the median difference (or at least report the IQRs already computed and phrase the verdict conditionally).
findings.verifier_reasoning: Test count verified exactly: _mwu is called at temporal_analysis.py:174 (Q1 pooled slope, x2 reaches), :190 (Q1 WSE per reach-year, 6 calls), :234-235 (Q2 WSE+slope, x2 reaches = 4) and :268-269 (Q3 WSE+slope, x2 reaches = 4) = 16 attempted; the JSON shows p_wse=None for both 2026 Q1 rows (n_low=1, caught by the len<3 guard at :140-141), leaving 14 valid p-values, all judged at raw 0.05 with no family-wise adjustment and all exported to JSON, the dashboard and the thesis. The Q3 verdict at :277-279 is confirmed to be a bare `abs(dwse) > abs(bw)` point-median comparison with no CI or bootstrap. Two corrections: the Q3 sample sizes are n=3 (Jun-2025) vs n=4 (Jun-2026), not 'n=4 vs ~4'; and the flip sensitivity is ~0.09 m (moving the single middle Jun-2025 Uyak pass up) or ~0.18 m (moving a middle Jun-2026 pass down), not '~0.1 m on a 2026 pass'. The substance survives: the June per-pass WSE spread is itself ~0.4 m (Uyak 2025: 30.151/30.513/30.550; 2026: 29.989/30.200/30.240/30.447), so a 0.09-0.18 m perturbation is well inside sampling noise and would flip the published 'within natural baseline' verdict that underpins the no-typhoon-signal conclusion. Severity 'medium' is right, not higher: the multiplicity issue only bites the single p=0.033 result (Q2's p=0.000/0.0019 survive Bonferroni, and every other p is >0.1), and correcting would only strengthen the paper's null conclusions — the real exposure is the uncertainty-free Q3 verdict.
findings.reproduction: grep -n '_mwu(' temporal_analysis.py -> calls at 174/190/234/235/268/269; JSON inspection -> 16 test slots, 2 with p=None; read temporal_results/temporal_metrics_per_pass.parquet and recomputed June medians per reach-year (Kanektok 2025 30.467 / 2026 30.381; Uyak 2025 30.513 / 2026 30.220), matching the JSON, then solved for the single-pass shift that flips |dwse| past |baseline_dwse| (Uyak: 0.383 vs 0.293 -> 0.09 m on the 2025 median pass, 0.18 m on a 2026 middle pass).

findings.title: D18: beta_floodplain.py depends on unversioned /tmp inputs — the documented ArcGIS β reproduction is irreproducible
findings.description: GDB = "/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb" (line 37) and the validation overlay reads "/tmp/original_beta.parquet" (line 147; run_B.py:189 reads the same path). Neither file exists now (verified: both absent), /tmp is volatile, and neither is tracked or documented with a recovery path in the repo. AVULSION_ANALYSIS.md:33 and :142 cite clean_and_complete.gdb as the source of the recovered ArcGIS result, and STATUS.md:98 cites beta_floodplain.py as the script that 'demonstrated the artifact'.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone (including the author, post-reboot) running `python3 DEM_Transects/beta_floodplain.py` to reproduce the writeup's two-zone β result gets an immediate failure opening /tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb; the provenance chain for a number cited in the thesis writeup is broken. The production arc pipeline (build_arc_B.py) is unaffected.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the recovered .gdb (or an exported GeoPackage of Avulsion_Lines_2/Guide_Lines_2) and original_beta.parquet into DEM_Transects/data/ or DEM_Transects/reference/ (they are small), or document the exact recovery procedure and update the paths.
findings.verifier_reasoning: Paths verified: DEM_Transects/beta_floodplain.py:37 `GDB = '/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb'`, used unguarded at :76 and :78 (`gpd.read_file(GDB, layer='Avulsion_Lines_2')`, `layer='Guide_Lines_2'`), so main() fails on the first line of work; :147 and run_B.py:189 read '/tmp/original_beta.parquet'. Both paths are absent from the filesystem now, /tmp is volatile, and neither file is tracked in DEM_Transects/data/ or DEM_Transects/reference/. AVULSION_ANALYSIS.md:33 and :142 do cite clean_and_complete.gdb as the source of the recovered β (median 0.96, H_AR 4.30 m) and STATUS.md:98 cites beta_floodplain.py. Three qualifiers pull the severity down to low. (1) The /tmp/original_beta.parquet reads at beta_floodplain.py:147 and run_B.py:189 are both wrapped in `if os.path.exists(...)`, so they degrade silently rather than failing — only the GDB read is a hard failure, contrary to the finding's 'neither file exists ... reads' framing. (2) STATUS.md:96-99 explicitly classifies beta_floodplain.py (and run_B.py) as 'Superseded / exploratory (kept for provenance)' — the current numbers come from build_arc_B.py, which the finding concedes is unaffected. (3) The source archive does still exist at /home/luke/Downloads/clean_and_complete.gdb.zip, so recovery is a single unzip away — it is just undocumented in the repo (no .md gives a path or recovery step for it). The defect is a genuine but low-impact reproducibility gap around a superseded negative-result script, not a broken production chain.
findings.reproduction: ls /tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb /tmp/original_beta.parquet -> both 'No such file or directory'; grep for the paths across DEM_Transects/*.py -> only beta_floodplain.py:37,147 and run_B.py:189; sed of beta_floodplain.py:75-78 shows the unguarded gpd.read_file(GDB, ...) and of run_B.py:188-191 the os.path.exists guard; find over /home/luke -> /home/luke/Downloads/clean_and_complete.gdb.zip present; ls DEM_Transects/data and DEM_Transects/reference -> no gdb/geopackage copy, no original_beta.parquet.

hygiene_unverified.title: Dashboard's LOESS detrending is index-space smoothing with density-dependent bandwidth
hygiene_unverified.description: The 'LOESS' branch of calculate_detrending is gaussian_filter1d over y sorted by x with sigma = 0.15*N/3 SAMPLES, not a local regression in distance: the physical bandwidth varies inversely with local point density along the reach and with total N (so the same selection sampled at a different size yields a different baseline, and residual outlier flags shift). Identical code is in thesis_figures/core.py:150. Currently unreachable in practice -- the dashboard hardcodes detrend_method = 'Polynomial (2nd order)' (line 1320) and Fig 7 uses the polynomial -- but it remains a selectable-looking method name that misdescribes the estimator.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Two selections with identical spatial support but different point counts (e.g. 30,000-point systematic sample vs full data) produce different LOESS baselines purely because sigma scales with N; residuals and Modified-Z outlier flags then differ. In a reach segment with 10x point density the effective smoothing window is 10x narrower in km, so the 'baseline' absorbs real local structure there while over-smoothing sparse segments.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Either remove the branch (it is dead with the hardcoded method) or implement distance-domain smoothing (e.g. fixed-km Gaussian on binned medians, as elsewhere in the codebase) and rename it honestly.

hygiene_unverified.title: np.round (half-to-even) vs DuckDB ROUND (half-away) bin points on .5 boundaries differently
hygiene_unverified.description: The pipeline mixes three rounding conventions for the same 0.1-km binning: numpy np.round in calculate_slope_profile (line 257; banker's rounding: round(2.5)=2), DuckDB ROUND in compute_finescale_pass_matrix (line 387; half-away-from-zero: ROUND(2.5)=3), and pandas Series.round in core.elevation_difference (core.py:378) and Fig 7's node binning (banker's). Verified: for x=0.25, np.round(x/0.1)=2 while DuckDB ROUND(x/0.1)=3, so the same point lands in different bins depending on code path.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Ran both against the archive: 24 real points in master_all_data.parquet fall exactly on a .5 boundary of the 0.1-km binning and are assigned to different bins by the numpy/pandas paths vs the DuckDB path. With 7.9M points the effect on any median is negligible today, but figures that juxtapose the two paths (fine-scale slope vs elevation-difference/slope-profile) are not bit-reproducible against each other at bin boundaries, and the discrepancy grows if binning is ever applied to already-quantized distances.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Standardize on FLOOR(dist_km/bin)+0.5*bin (half-open bins) or a single rounding convention implemented in one shared helper used by both SQL and Python paths.

hygiene_unverified.title: compute_finescale_slope is dead code and silently diverges from core's gating
hygiene_unverified.description: compute_finescale_slope is never called anywhere in dashboard_swot.py (the Fine-Scale tab uses compute_finescale_pass_matrix + _fine_aggregate directly and applies its own n>=3 display gate). It also aggregates with _fine_aggregate's default min_passes=0, whereas the 'verbatim' counterpart thesis_figures/core.py:finescale_slope_profile defaults min_passes=3 -- so if this wrapper were ever used, its output would include 1-2-pass bins that Fig 9 masks, violating the module's 'keep them in lockstep' contract.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A future caller uses compute_finescale_slope expecting the tab/Fig-9 behavior: bins imaged by only 1-2 passes return a 'median' equal to that single pass's slope with a zero-width band, instead of NaN. On the full archive this affects the sparse-coverage bins where n < 3 (present at reach edges and gap regions).
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Delete the wrapper, or make it call _fine_aggregate(r['mat'], min_passes=3) and actually use it in the tab.

hygiene_unverified.title: calculate_detrending crashes or warns on degenerate (<3 point) inputs
hygiene_unverified.description: load_detrend_frame only guards len(bdf)==0 before calling calculate_detrending. stats.linregress raises ValueError for a single point and returns NaN slope for 2 identical-x points; np.polynomial.Polynomial.fit with fewer points than degree+1 raises or produces a rank-deficient warning with an unstable baseline. The same applies to thesis core.calculate_detrending (core.py:126).
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A dashboard selection whose where_clause matches exactly 1 row (a single pass clipped to a tiny reach subset -- achievable via the pass/reach filters) reaches calculate_detrending with n=1: scipy raises ValueError('Inputs must not be empty' / needs 2 points), which surfaces as an uncaught exception in the Detrended Profile tab instead of the existing friendly 'No data available' warning.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Extend the guard to require a minimum point count (e.g. n >= 10, matching the slope tab's existing threshold) before fitting, returning the empty-data path otherwise.

hygiene_unverified.title: Ice-season warning renders only in the data-reload branch and vanishes on the next full rerun
hygiene_unverified.description: The 'Ice season data included' st.warning (lines 1346–1355) sits inside the `if "viz_df" not in st.session_state or viz_sig != selection_sig:` reload branch (line 1334). On any subsequent full rerun with the same selection the cached else-branch runs and the warning is never emitted again, even though winter passes are still selected and every chart still shows ice-contaminated WSE.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: User selects a December pass on the welcome page and launches: the warning appears once. They then box-select points on the Gradient Profile (on_select='rerun') or move the Cross-Sections radius slider — both trigger a full rerun that takes the cached path — and the scientific caution about 0.5–2+ m ice-inflated WSE silently disappears while the ice data remains in every tab.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Move the ice_selected check and st.warning outside the reload branch (it depends only on selected_pass_dates, which is available on every run).

hygiene_unverified.title: Fine-scale n_passes and the reliability gate count passes that contributed no data
hygiene_unverified.description: In compute_finescale_pass_matrix, passes with fewer than 5 grid bins are skipped (`if len(ix) < 5: continue`) but still occupy an all-NaN column in `mat` and are counted in `passes`/`n_passes`. The legend label '(N passes)', the near-bifurcation table's 'Passes' column, and the MIN_PASSES_RELIABLE=10 warning gate (line 2832) therefore overstate the number of passes actually supporting the profile.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A selection of 10 passes where 3 imaged fewer than 5 usable 0.1 km bins passes the 'Too few passes' gate (min pass_counts = 10 >= 10) and the chart legend claims 10 passes, while only 7 columns of the matrix contain any slope values — the exact selection-artifact condition the warning exists to catch.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Count n_passes (and drive the gate) from columns with at least one finite value, e.g. np.isfinite(mat).any(axis=0).sum().

hygiene_unverified.title: Return-to-Homepage comment claims pass checkbox states are preserved, but Streamlit garbage-collects them
hygiene_unverified.description: The comment at 1274–1277 says '(pass_{date} widget states are preserved so the checkboxes still reflect the last choice.)'. They are not: the pass_{d} keys are widget-bound checkbox keys that only render on the welcome page, and Streamlit deletes widget-keyed session state at the end of any run in which the widget is not rendered — which the code itself acknowledges at 1290–1294 (the reason confirmed_pass_dates exists). Since Return-to-Homepage also pops confirmed_pass_dates and pass_defaults_initialized remains set, the welcome page renders with every checkbox unchecked and no re-defaulting.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: User launches the dashboard with a custom pass selection, interacts (any second full rerun GCs the pass_ keys), clicks 'Return to Homepage': the 'Choose Specific Dates' expander shows 0 passes selected instead of the last choice, and 'Launch Dashboard' warns 'Please select at least one pass'. No wrong data is shown (the fallback protects the dashboard), but the comment documents behavior that does not exist and the welcome page loses the user's selection.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Either restore checkbox state on the welcome page from confirmed_pass_dates before rendering the checklist (and only pop confirmed after restoring), or fix the comment.

hygiene_unverified.title: Reach names are interpolated into SQL without quoting/escaping
hygiene_unverified.description: rivers_sql = "'" + "','".join(selected_reaches) + "'" embeds Reach_Name values taken from the parquet (SELECT DISTINCT Reach_Name) directly into every WHERE clause with no escaping. Not user-controllable today (values are the two fixed reach constants, verified in the data: only Kanektok_River and Uyak_Creek), but any future dataset whose reach name contains an apostrophe (e.g. O'Malley_Creek) breaks every query built from where_clause, and the same where_clause string is a cache key, so the malformed SQL is also cached.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A third reach named "St. Mary's_Slough" is ingested: render_dashboard's COUNT query throws a DuckDB parser error on every launch and the dashboard st.stop()s.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Escape single quotes (r.replace("'", "''")) when building rivers_sql, or use DuckDB parameter binding for the reach list.

hygiene_unverified.title: Stage-invariance correlation is computed but never shown (temporal tab)
hygiene_unverified.description: In Chart 2 of the Temporal Results tab, r = float(np.corrcoef(d["wse_ref_m"], d["slope_cm_km"])[0, 1]) is computed per reach but never used — corr_txt only reports the median slope. The caption's claim that 'the bands are flat' (i.e. slope is stage-invariant) is exactly what r would quantify, so the supporting statistic was evidently intended to be displayed and silently is not.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A reader of the tab (or a committee member) asks for the correlation backing the 'water level has almost no effect' claim; the page presents none, although the code computes it and then discards it on every render.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Include r in corr_txt (e.g. 'usually about {med:.0f} cm/km, r = {r:+.2f}') or delete the computation.

hygiene_unverified.title: Exported slope_calc is a density-biased pixel OLS, fit to tile-truncated and MAD-amputated profiles
hygiene_unverified.description: slope_calc (lines 343-347) is an OLS fit over raw pixels per reach-granule: (a) it is density-weighted (the 3,735 px at Uyak node 35 vs ~200 px/node upstream on 2023-09-01 pull the fit toward the downstream reach — the exact bias the node-binned Theil-Sen reference gradient was introduced to fix), and (b) it is computed on whatever survives the upstream defects: on the 50 pass-571 dates it is a 'reach gradient' fit over only km 30.7-35.1, and on the 46 MAD-amputated Uyak dates over the truncated lower profile. These values are stored in every daily CSV, kept by KEEP_COLUMNS into the master parquet, and shipped to the dashboard, where they are indistinguishable from full-reach gradients.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: For 2023-11-03 Uyak, slope_calc in the master is an OLS over km 20-36 only (upstream amputated); for any pass-571 date it is an OLS over km 30.7-35.1 of Kanektok. A dashboard user or script averaging slope_calc across passes mixes full-reach and 5-km-stub 'gradients' with no flag distinguishing them.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Either drop slope_calc from the export (the reference-gradient artifact is the authoritative slope) or store it alongside lo_km/hi_km/n so consumers can gate on coverage, mirroring the refgrad gate.

hygiene_unverified.title: Unparseable granule names collapse onto one 'Unknown_Date' CSV and would crash compute_reference_gradient
hygiene_unverified.description: If the timestamp regex walk fails (line 204-216), formatted_date becomes 'Unknown_Date': every such granule writes/overwrites the single file Unknown_Date_data.csv (line 352), and extract_date_from_granule returns None so the skip check never blocks reprocessing. At rebuild, rows with Pass_Date='Unknown_Date' pass the KNOWN_BAD filter and column pruning, then `pd.to_datetime(df['Pass_Date'])` at line 410 raises on the unparseable string, aborting the reference-gradient step after the master files are already written (master and refgrad artifacts go out of sync). Not currently triggered (all 189 CSVs are date-named), but a PGE naming change or a differently-formatted collection would hit it.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A granule named without a 15-char YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS token is processed -> Unknown_Date_data.csv written -> next rebuild: master parquet includes Pass_Date='Unknown_Date' rows, then compute_reference_gradient raises ValueError/DateParseError at pd.to_datetime, so reference_gradient_per_pass.parquet is left stale relative to the new master.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Treat an unparseable date as a hard skip (log and continue) instead of processing under a sentinel name; or validate Pass_Date with `pd.to_datetime(..., errors='coerce')` and drop/report NaT rows at rebuild.

hygiene_unverified.title: XOVERCAL_SUSPECT_MASK and two loaded quality columns are dead; comment overstates the applied filter
hygiene_unverified.description: XOVERCAL_SUSPECT_MASK (bit 6, line 28) is defined with a comment ('bit masks for geolocation_qual', plural) but never applied — only XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK is used (line 293). classification_qual (line 251) and height_cor_xover_qual (line 253) are extracted from every granule and carried through the polygon clip but never referenced by any filter or export. A reader of the config block (or of SCIENTIFIC_METHODOLOGY.md text derived from it) would conclude suspect-crossover pixels are excluded; they are not.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Pixels with geolocation_qual bit 6 set (crossover cal suspect) pass all filters and enter the master with no record; anyone documenting the QC chain from the constants block reports a filter that does not run.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Either apply the suspect mask (`& (XOVERCAL_SUSPECT_MASK | XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK) == 0`) deliberately, or delete the unused constant and the two unused column loads and note the decision where the other disabled filters are documented (lines 298-303).

hygiene_unverified.title: Failed and empty downloads vanish without accounting; failures re-attempted every run with no record
hygiene_unverified.description: `if not files: return None` (line 220) drops a granule with no message at all; the catch-all except (line 359) reduces any error (network, NetCDF corruption, the astype crash above) to one scrolling tqdm line. main() tracks processed_count and skipped_count but no failed_count, and the summary (line 596) plus the immediately-following master rebuild give no signal that granules are missing. Granules that legitimately yield no polygon data also never write a checkpoint, so they are re-downloaded on every single resume run (53 pass-265 granules and ~10 others, i.e. ~60+ full PIXC downloads repeated per run).
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A transient Earthdata outage during a 400-granule run fails 30 downloads; the run ends with '📊 Summary: 340 new, 30 skipped'-style output that never mentions the 30 failures, and the master is rebuilt and published incomplete. Verified the no-yield case from CMR-vs-disk: the 53 pass-265 dates have no CSVs, so every resume re-downloads all 53.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Count and print failures in the summary (and exit nonzero or warn before rebuilding if any); write a zero-byte or sentinel checkpoint (e.g., `{date}_empty.marker`) for granules that legitimately produce no polygon data.

hygiene_unverified.title: Polygon file with missing CRS is silently assumed EPSG:4326
hygiene_unverified.description: `if gdf.crs and gdf.crs.to_string() != 'EPSG:4326'` reprojects only when a CRS is present; a shapefile missing its .prj loads with crs=None and is used as-is with no warning. If the polygons were in a projected CRS (e.g., the ArcticDEM work uses polar stereographic), coordinates in meters would never intersect the lon/lat pixel cloud and every granule would 'process' to zero points — a silent all-data-lost mode rather than an error. The current river_poly.zip is verified fine (EPSG:4326, fields id/Name resolve via the id path in resolve_poly_name), so this is latent.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: User regenerates river_poly.zip from a GIS export that drops the .prj (crs=None) while the geometry is in EPSG:3413 meters: load_polygons prints '✅ Loaded 2 polygons', every granule returns None (no rough-bbox matches), and the run completes 'successfully' having ingested nothing.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Fail hard when gdf.crs is None (or set_crs with an explicit, logged assumption), and sanity-check total_bounds against valid lon/lat ranges before searching.

hygiene_unverified.title: Snap-window 'clipped' QC flag can miss wall-limited picks because the center is the median of the deepest-percentile points
hygiene_unverified.description: The wall flag is `abs(k_off) >= SNAP_WIN_KAN_M - ARC_STEP_M` (>= 73 m), but the reported center is not an extreme sample: it is `np.median(arc_m[search & (z <= thr)])` over the deepest-P2 points (comment says 'centroid', code is median). Re-running the snap on the real raster: the deepest-percentile selection is typically 2 points (median count 2) with positional spread up to 74 m, so when the deepest terrain is truncated by the +/-75 m wall, the median can sit well inside the wall (e.g. one point at the wall, one 40 m inside -> offset ~55 m) and the pick evades the clipped flag while still being wall-limited. Also, the actual linspace sample spacing is arc_len/(n-1) > 2.0 m, so the threshold win - ARC_STEP_M is marginally too high for a pick at the last in-window sample. In the committed data 6 Kanektok / 5 Uyak arcs are flagged and offsets reach 73.9 m, so the flag mostly works; the failure mode is under-reporting in the migration QC, not a wrong WSE (measured WSE is insensitive, and one arc, R=33.5, already has its median-center 52 m from the window argmin).
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: An arc where the DEM channel migrated beyond the +/-75 m window but a secondary low sits 40 m inside it: the P2 selection straddles both, the median lands ~35-55 m from the prior, kan_snap_clipped stays False, and the 'AT THE WALL on N% of arcs' QC statistic understates how many crest windows are anchored on a lower-bound position.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Flag when the search window itself was truncated (lo/hi hit the wall AND any selected deep point lies within one sample spacing of the wall), rather than thresholding the median offset.

hygiene_unverified.title: Shared spherical/haversine radial coordinate understates true ground distance by ~0.36%, inflating all per-km gradients by the same factor
hygiene_unverified.description: dest()/dist_bear() (R=6371.0088) and SWOT_Pull/DEM_Pull haversine (R=6371.0) are mutually consistent — a DEM arc point at nominal R has archive-convention dist_km exactly R (verified: 0.0 m mismatch at all tested radii/bearings) — but the spherical convention compresses real WGS84 distances at this latitude: a point truly 34.5 km from the anchor (pyproj Geod, WGS84) gets dist_km = 34.375 km (-0.36%). The spherical destination also sits 10-125 m from the true geodesic destination over 3-34.5 km. Because the shortfall is a uniform scale factor applied identically to both rivers and to both SWOT and DEM, all comparative conclusions (Uyak-Kanektok, beta, superelevation) are unaffected; but absolute per-km numbers quoted in the thesis (e.g. canonical gradients 195.4 / 191.7 cm/km) are systematically ~0.36% high (~0.7 cm/km) because the denominator km is short.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Quoting 'Kanektok gradient 195.4 cm/km' as a physical slope: the true along-radial slope is ~194.7 cm/km. Any external comparison against a slope computed with proper geodesic or projected distances carries a built-in 0.36% offset.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Either document the spherical-distance convention where gradients are quoted, or switch dist_km/dest to pyproj.Geod (WGS84) everywhere at once — never in only one component, since the current correctness rests on every component using the same sphere.

hygiene_unverified.title: swot_arc_reference builds the 'archive' stats from dashboard_data.parquet (60 open-water passes), not the full 188-pass archive its docstring claims
hygiene_unverified.description: The docstring says the script 'Condenses the full SWOT pixel archive', but SWOT_CANDIDATES prefers ROOT/dashboard_data.parquet, which contains 60 passes (2.4M rows, Apr-Jul open-water seasons 2023-2026), while batch_outputs/master_all_data_part_*.parquet holds 188 passes (7.9M rows) including winter. Excluding ice-season passes is almost certainly the right science, but it is an undocumented consequence of which file happens to sit in ROOT: the published 'stage distribution' (median/p10/p90 per radius) and diff_pass_paired stats are open-water-season statistics, and they silently change if dashboard_data.parquet is swapped for a different release subset. The 'median stage' the thesis superelevation is quoted at is the Apr-Jul median, not an annual one.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A future rebuild after dashboard_data.parquet is regenerated with a different date range (the file has already grown from the documented 29 passes to 60) silently shifts swot_*_wse_med_m and hence every headline superelevation value, with no provenance recorded in the output parquet.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: State the open-water-season restriction in the docstring, and write the source filename + pass count/date range into the parquet (or print-log them) so the reference artifact carries its provenance.

hygiene_unverified.title: beta_floodplain.py depends on unversioned /tmp inputs that no longer exist, so the published beta reproduction cannot be re-run
hygiene_unverified.description: GDB = '/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb' and the validation overlay path '/tmp/original_beta.parquet' point at volatile /tmp locations; neither exists now (verified). The script that produced the beta_floodplain.parquet numbers and the rebuild-vs-original validation figure is therefore not reproducible from the repository — gpd.read_file raises immediately. The hardcoded x-axis in the validation overlay (ox = arange(len(o)) * (26.68/len(o))) also assumes a fixed transect count/extent that is only implicit.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Anyone (including the author after a reboot clears /tmp) running `python3 DEM_Transects/beta_floodplain.py` to regenerate or check the thesis beta numbers gets a DriverError: '/tmp/clean_and_complete.gdb' does not exist, and the recovered-ArcGIS comparison cannot be reproduced.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Move the recovered gdb (or an exported GeoPackage of Avulsion_Lines_2 / Guide_Lines_2) and original_beta.parquet into DEM_Transects/data or DEM_Transects/reference and point the constants there.

hygiene_unverified.title: DEM_Pull assumes river_poly.zip is EPSG:4326 without reprojecting
hygiene_unverified.description: main() reads the polygon and uses gdf.total_bounds directly as degree coordinates for the ee.Geometry.Rectangle, and sample_dem_within_polygons masks the EPSG:4326 raster with row.geometry, with no .to_crs() anywhere. It works only because river_poly.zip happens to be EPSG:4326 (verified). DEM_2m_Pull.py handles the same file correctly (g3413 = gdf.to_crs(MOSAIC_CRS)). If the polygon file is ever re-exported from ArcGIS in EPSG:3413 (like every other layer in this project), the GEE region becomes a degenerate rectangle in meter-coordinates interpreted as degrees and rio_mask returns empty/garbage rather than an obvious CRS error.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Replace river_poly.zip with a 3413-projected export: export_dem_from_gee builds a Rectangle at e.g. lon=-2998526 which GEE rejects or wraps, and if the old tif exists the masking step silently yields 'no valid pixels' for both rivers.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Add gdf = gdf.to_crs(4326) after reading, mirroring DEM_2m_Pull.py.

hygiene_unverified.title: Typhoon spatial-delta chart's fixed y-range clips the largest real WSE change (+0.68 m) while the caption claims the line 'hugs zero'
hygiene_unverified.description: Chart 4 sets yaxis_range=[-0.5, 0.5] unconditionally. The committed temporal_q3_profile.parquet contains dwse up to +0.676 m: three Kanektok bins at 33.5, 34.0, 34.5 km are +0.528, +0.676, +0.538 m — beyond the axis, so their markers are cut off at the frame. The caption above the chart states 'the line stays flat and hugs zero — no spot along the river shows a storm scar', with no disclosure that the axis truncates the biggest excursion.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: Loaded temporal_results/temporal_q3_profile.parquet: 3 of 142 rows exceed |0.5| m (max +0.676 at 34.0 km). A reader of the tab sees a line exiting the top of the frame near the mouth but cannot see its peak, and is told the profile hugs zero everywhere. The excursion is at the tidal mouth (arguably tidal aliasing, and consistent with the 'damage was coastal' narrative), but it is hidden rather than shown-and-explained.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Drop the fixed range (autoscale) or widen it to cover the data, and add a sentence noting the coastal-end excursion and its likely tidal origin; alternatively trim the tidal mouth as the fine-scale tab does (34 km) and say so.

hygiene_unverified.title: Typhoon spatial-delta chart is the only distance-axis figure without the reversed x-axis convention

hygiene_unverified.title: astype(int) on geolocation_qual crashes the whole granule if the column is partially NaN
hygiene_unverified.description: Line 292 guards with df_exact['geolocation_qual'].notna().any() (ANY, not ALL), then line 293 does .astype(int) on the float column. If even one pixel decodes as NaN (xarray converts _FillValue in the uint32 flag to NaN), pandas raises ValueError('Cannot convert non-finite values (NA or inf) to integer'). The raise is swallowed by the broad except at line 359, which prints one 'Failed' line and returns None — so the ENTIRE granule (all reaches, all pixels) is dropped, no daily CSV is written, and every future resumable run retries and fails identically, leaving a permanent silent hole in the archive.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: pd.Series([64.0, np.nan]).astype(int) -> ValueError (verified behavior). A PIXC granule with one fill-valued geolocation_qual pixel inside the AOI: cross-track filter passes, line 293 raises, tqdm.write prints '❌ <date>: Failed - Cannot convert non-finite values...' among hundreds of progress lines, and that pass is absent from the master with no flag anywhere. Cannot confirm an occurrence in the current archive (qual columns are not exported to the daily CSVs), but the crash path is deterministic given a single NaN.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: Treat NaN qual as its own category: mask = df_exact['geolocation_qual'].fillna(0).astype('int64') & XOVERCAL_MISSING_MASK == 0 (or drop NaN-qual pixels explicitly), and narrow the except so ingestion errors are counted/reported per granule.

hygiene_unverified.title: Silent load_tide=0 fallback with no warning or flag column (currently never triggered)
hygiene_unverified.description: Lines 246-247: if neither load_tide_fes nor load_tide_height exists in a granule, load_tide is silently set to scalar 0 and WSE (line 262) simply omits that correction, with no warning, no flag column, and no way to distinguish 'correction genuinely ~0' from 'correction missing' downstream except an exact-zero test. Verified against the full archive: 0 of 7,895,912 rows have load_tide == 0 exactly (range -0.036..+0.028 m, mean |.| 1.0 cm), so the fallback has never fired on real data and no published number is affected — the suspicion holds as a latent hazard only. If a future PIXC version renames the variable, every new pass would carry a systematic ~+/-1-3.5 cm WSE bias, comparable to the seasonal WSE signals (0.2-0.5 m) being resolved at the cm level.
hygiene_unverified.failure_scenario: A PIXC version E renames load_tide_fes: all new granules ingest with load_tide=0, WSE shifts ~1-3 cm relative to the older record, and the temporal analysis interprets the step as an interannual water-level change. Nothing in logs or outputs flags the substitution.
hygiene_unverified.suggested_fix: tqdm.write a per-granule warning and/or set load_tide to NaN (failing loudly downstream) instead of 0; optionally add a boolean load_tide_missing column.

hygiene_unverified.title: Cross-track filter silently skipped when the variable is absent/all-NaN
hygiene_unverified.description: Line 281: the 10-60 km cross-track gate runs only if the column exists and has any non-NaN value; otherwise the granule proceeds unfiltered (nadir-gap and far-swath pixels retained) with no message — the skip is indistinguishable from a pass. Confirmed the code path; assessed impact as latent: cross_track is a core PIXC variable present in all Version-D granules, the column is unconditionally created (line 252) so the 'in columns' clause is always true, and the daily CSVs don't export it so an occurrence can't be audited after the fact. No evidence any archived pass was ingested unfiltered. Note the mirror behavior is silently strict: pixels whose cross_track is NaN while others are valid are dropped by the >= comparison without being counted in the log line.
